conclusion: The joint 7-application-worker plus 1-dedicated-ingress treatment reduced observed client socket queue/drop pressure. B and D both passed 3/3, so this does not demonstrate a reliability fix, identify the unique causal mechanism, or establish a server performance improvement.
scope: Client-only diagnostic, never server performance acceptance. B uses eight shared application workers; D uses seven application workers plus one dedicated endpoint ingress worker. Both have the same eight-core allowance, CPUs8–15. D jointly changes pool allocation and runtime isolation; it does not isolate either factor alone. The main coordinator retains CPUs8–15 in both arms. One shared UDP endpoint and the requested4MiB receive buffer are unchanged. D application placement is enforced at the ready gate; pre-ready samples are startup observations, not proof of the 9–15 application partition. Run all six fixed cases through ordinary failures; three repetitions do not establish a failure rate or automatic winner. Passing while generating less offered work is insufficient. Observer timing, CPU and RSS are diagnostic, not ordinary benchmarks.
stopping_rule: Run all six cases; ordinary workload failure does not stop the series. Infrastructure errors abort with partial status.

generation_semantics: Generated is counted after successful local send completion, not server receipt. Lag is sampled before the send against its schedule; last_submit_ms is after send completion. Histogram p50/p99 are bucket upper bounds; max_ms is exact for observed samples. A 4-second cutoff can leave a few planned updates ungenerated; every actual count is reported without an invented completeness threshold.
limits: All three B controls and all three D cases passed. Three rotated repetitions cannot establish a failure-rate improvement or show that the earlier intermittent failure is fixed.

D jointly reallocates one of eight application workers to a dedicated endpoint runtime and isolates that runtime on CPU 8. It does not isolate runtime placement from application-pool size; a 7-worker shared-runtime control was not run.

D and B share the same total runtime-worker/core budget on CPUs 8-15. Both also have a coordinator thread allowed on CPUs 8-15. This is not an additional ninth runtime worker or eight-plus-one CPU treatment.
Connection/application futures still use the application runtime. Thread counters do not directly attribute individual migrating futures or prove exact endpoint wake delay.

One shared UDP socket, requested 4 MiB receive buffer, certificate pin, traffic, pacing and verification are unchanged. Sampled queue accounting is kernel socket memory accounting, not application payload or complete kernel memory.

UDP peaks and cumulative drops are observed at actual sample times; sub-sample peaks or bursts can be missed. The socket lifetime window includes setup/cleanup; ready-to-measured drop deltas are reported separately.
CPU ticks are quantized and per-thread reads are sequential. OS schedstat wait is runnable-thread wait, not Tokio future wait; disabled schedstats cannot establish absence of starvation.
Requested 4 ms UDP and 40 ms CPU cadence are targets; actual gaps and collector costs are retained. Observer-instrumented CPU/RSS/timing is not an ordinary server benchmark.
Cleanup receipts establish normal close counts and zero retained relay accounting; successful process exit bounds thread lifetime. They are not a per-allocation or kernel-object leak proof.

D intentionally retains the ingress guard through the done gate; it signals and joins the ingress thread after that gate is continued. Teardown is supported by source lifetime and successful process exit, without a separate post-join event.
Historical individual source-file references describe archived source. Canonical B/C/D archives were verified; the shared build tree is currently restored to C while its target cache can contain D.
causal_findings: B 3/3 and D 3/3 pass with zero unreceived generated deliveries, duplicate/order errors and refusal traces. The experiment does not distinguish their failure rate.
Every B case records client UDP drops and a sampled RX queue peak above 6.6 MB; every D case records zero client UDP drops and a peak below 0.94 MB. Server UDP drops are zero in all six.

The lower observed client pressure supports further investigation of endpoint/runtime scheduling and contention. It does not isolate scheduling from the changed application-pool allocation or identify a particular lock.

Private generation leaves only 59-224 source updates ungenerated out of 1,024,000; B3 also leaves 1 of 4,000 fanout source updates ungenerated. Exact fractions, lag and last submissions are reported rather than excluding small cutoff differences.
Server CPU does not improve in these diagnostic captures, and all ordinary server-performance acceptance still uses the original fixed client A.
